To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have derived a link between the GPDs, which are defined in the infinite momentum frame, and the uPDFs, which are the parton distributions in the light-front dynamics, and have shown that the GPDs are entirely determined from the parton conserved light-cone wave function overlaps.
the effective light-cone models provide an efficient tool for the calculation of GPDs from uPDFs and vice versa and that transversity GPDs are not small.
GPDs and uPDFs can be obtained from LCWFs and, in turn, that the LCWF overlap method can be employed to model GPDs in terms of uPDFs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the development of models for GPDs and uPDFs, which are based on a consistent description of the underlying light-cone wave function structure.

the following questions: 1) What is the connection between GPDs and LCWFs? 2) How can GPDs be modeled in a consistent way? 3) What are the constraints among the GPDs? 4) What are the transversity distributions and how do they depend on the model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LCWFs and their overlaps are the most fundamental quantities to describe parton distributions in the nucleon.
GPDs can indeed be modeled in terms of effective LCWFs, and that the resulting models provide a link between GPDs and uPDFs.

the present models of LCWFs are able to describe the experimental data for both GPDs and uPDFs, but they cannot be considered as a unique and universal description of the nonperturbative QCD dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a model-independent and systematic way of calculating GPDs and uPDFs from the same LCWFs, and we also provide model constraints among GPCs.
we have established the link between GPDs and uPDFs.
we have established a model-independent link between GPDs and uPDFs, and that we can provide a model-independent link for transversity GPDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GPDs are not independent quantities and can be entirely obtained in terms of the effective two-body LCWFs.
GPDs and uPDFs can be obtained from the same effective LCWF model.
GPDs are not only a tool for studying nucleon tomography.
